lines: +# Fidelity check: settled rule and why
+## The rule
+`check <run_dir>` loads every `train_data/*.pt` dump, ignores any launch
+command, and **holds** the change (exit 1) if any gate below fires; otherwise
+it **passes** it (exit 0). If there are no readable dumps or no
+policy-generated (loss-masked) tokens, it holds. It prints exactly one line
+with the reason and the measured statistics.
+1. **Sibling independence (primary gate).** Samples are grouped by an MD5 of
+   their prompt tokens (`tokens[: total_length - response_length]` within
+   each dump). For every sibling pair, take the pair's common response
+   prefix and sum the *trainer* log-probs (`log_probs`) of the generated
+   (loss-mask 1) tokens inside that prefix. That sum is the log conditional
+   probability that a second, independent draw from the trainer policy
+   follows exactly that prefix. **Hold if more than 2% of pairs (at least
+   3 pairs, at least 30 pairs total) share a prefix with sum < -20**
+   (probability < 2e-9). Backstop: hold if exact-duplicate generated-token
+   pairs exceed 20% or near-duplicate (>=90% common prefix) pairs exceed 25%.
+2. **Gross distribution-drift backstops** over loss-masked tokens only
+   (rollout log-probs are a 0.0 placeholder on tool-output tokens, so
+   unmasked tokens must never enter any statistic). With
+   `d = log_probs (trainer) - rollout_log_probs (engine)`, hold if any of:
+   turn-0 "decision-token" (-2 <= rollout logp < -0.05) mean |d| > 0.075
+   (at least 1000 such tokens); per-sample-mean k3
+   (tokens faithfully sampled from the reported engine distribution give
+   E[train/rollout probability ratio] = 1 exactly).
+3. **Severe sampling-support distortion at step 0** (only when the earliest
+   dump is rollout 0 and has >= 15k masked tokens; step 0 is always the
+   base policy, before any update): hold if
+   (support truncated far beyond top-p 0.98), or if
+   `frac(rollout logp < -10) > 0.008` (sampler emitting tokens the engine
+   itself rates ultra-unlikely, e.g. draft-token leaks or misaligned
+   log-probs).
+Nothing else is gated. In particular the check does **not** threshold the
+dashboard's global train/rollout `absdiff` or `k3` at anywhere near their
+healthy-run values, and does not gate reward, pass rate, response length,
+or the zero-reward-std group fraction (reported for context only).
+## What the trainer assumes
+In this recipe the GRPO loss in Miles (`policy_loss_function` in
+`miles/backends/training_utils/loss_hub/losses.py`) uses
+trainer-recomputed `log_probs` as the old-policy denominator:
+`--use-rollout-logprobs` and `--use-tis` are off, so engine
+`rollout_log_probs` feed only the dashboard metrics. There is **no
+importance correction** for behaviour/trainer mismatch. The dump's
+`log_probs` are computed by the actor before the step's update
+(`compute_log_prob` in `miles/backends/megatron_utils/actor.py`), i.e.
+exactly the distribution GRPO assumes generated the samples. So the
+contract is: for each prompt, four **independent** samples from that
+trainer distribution (temperature 1), from which group-normalised
+advantages are computed. Two ways an engine change can break learning
+while looking fine token-by-token are therefore (a) destroying
+independence/contrast inside a group, and (b) sampling from a
+materially different distribution than the trainer's.
+## Why the dashboard panel cannot be the gate
+The known-bad run (`--sglang-enable-prefill-only-deterministic-inference`)
+has *better* panel numbers than a healthy baseline (abs-diff 0.016 vs
+0.025, k3 0.0039 vs 0.0074), because its per-token logits are fine. Its
+failure is visible only at group level: pass@1 0.28 -> pass@4 0.31 across
+steps, 87-90% of groups with identical rewards, grad norm ~0.36 vs
+~1.1-1.35 for baselines, pass@1 0.28 -> 0.34 while baselines go
+Conversely the panel false-alarms on healthy runs. On identical-config
+runs its aggregates swing widely (dashboard base seeds: abs-diff 0.025
+vs 0.0076; per step within the lr-0 null screens the sample-mean
+abs-diff ranges 0.007-0.029). ~65% of generated tokens have rollout
+prob > 0.99 (median |d| ~ 1e-5), so global means are dominated by a
+small, content-dependent tail of low-probability tokens and by how many
+late-turn tokens a run happens to contain (mismatch grows ~4x from turn
+0 to turn >= 3 even on the production engine, from decode-vs-teacher-
+forced GDN scan/state-restore differences). Any tight global threshold
+fires on seed, prompt mix, and training progress, not on engine fidelity.
+## The known-bad mechanism (why gate 1 exists)
+`--sglang-enable-prefill-only-deterministic-inference` sets
+`enable_deterministic_inference = True` inside SGLang
+(`ServerArgs._handle_deterministic_inference`), which switches sampling
+to seeded Gumbel sampling keyed by (sampling_seed, position)
+(`Sampler.multinomial_with_seed`). But Miles only assigns distinct
+per-sample seeds (`group_sampling_seeds = [rollout_seed + i]`) when
+**its** `sglang_enable_deterministic_inference` arg is set; the
+prefill-only flag never sets it. SGLang then defaults every request's
+seed to 42 (`SamplingBatchInfo.from_schedule_batch`). All four siblings
+share the prompt, the seed, and the position stream, so they sample the
+same trajectory until batch-composition numerics eventually flip a
+token. Measured on the lr-0 screen of this flag (screened on this box):
+70.7% of sibling pairs have byte-identical generated tokens, 83.8%
+share a < 2e-9-probability prefix, 90% of groups have zero reward
+variance — while abs-diff (0.0132) and k3 (0.0034) sit inside the
+healthy range. The full `--sglang-enable-deterministic-inference`
+screen restores distinct seeds and is indistinguishable from prod on
+gate 1 (0.000 impossible prefixes), which is why the gate is computed
+from samples, never from flag names.
+Gate 1's calibration needs no reference run: under independent sampling
+a shared prefix of trainer log-prob < -20 occurs with probability
+< 2e-9 per pair. Across all 15 lr-0 screens and 5 training probes below
+(~30k pairs), healthy runs have **zero** such pairs (their most extreme
+shared prefix is > -9), including trained-policy runs where raw exact
+duplicates legitimately reach 1.6% — those are short, near-deterministic
+trajectories whose whole-sequence trainer log-prob is only -1 to -4.
+Weighting duplication by trainer probability makes the gate invariant
+to seed, prompt mix, and how sharp the policy has become during training.
